## Summary

The `abpai-skills-codex` skill is a **documentation-only guide** (a single `SKILL.md`, no scripts, no binaries, no setup/install steps, no embedded executable code). Its sole function is to instruct the agent on how to construct and run **OpenAI Codex CLI** (`codex exec` / `codex resume`) commands for code analysis and automated edits.

**What I observed:**
- The skill contains no setup scripts, network calls, downloads, or `curl|bash`-style instructions. It is inert text.
- The `codex` CLI is **not installed** in this sandbox (`command not found`, exit 127), so no actual Codex command can execute. `node v18.20.8` / `npm 10.8.2` are present but Codex is not in any global module path.
- No Codex auth/config is present (`OPENAI_API_KEY`, `CODEX_API_KEY`, `~/.codex/config.toml` all absent).
- I ran the only documented validation command (`codex --version`) and a representative read-only example command — both fail cleanly because the binary is missing. No network, no filesystem mutation outside `/home/appuser/workdir`.

**Safety notes (benign, but worth flagging):** The skill recommends `2>/dev/null` "to suppress thinking tokens" (suppresses stderr — reduces visibility but not deceptive), and documents high-impact flags `--full-auto`, `--sandbox danger-full-access`, `--skip-git-repo-check`. Notably, the skill *itself* instructs asking permission before high-impact flags — so it is self-limiting rather than evasive. No instruction asked me to bypass safety, hide behavior, exfiltrate, or run remote code.
